transcript.text: Hi, our integrated fridge freezer (behind a kitchen door) - the fridge is around 10 degrees but the freezer seems ok. We had a power cut a week ago, not sure if related. Rented flat, can't really take it out.

A fridge section at 10°C while the freezer stays cold usually points to an airflow issue rather than a loss of refrigerant. In frost-free models, a fan moves cold air from the freezer into the fridge; if that fan has failed or if ice/food is blocking the vent between them, the fridge will warm up while the freezer remains fine. Could you confirm if your unit is frost-free (auto-defrost)? If it is, please check two things: first, ensure no food is pressing against the air vents on the back wall of the fridge section; second, listen closely when the door is open to see if you can hear a small fan running inside. This will help us decide if it's a simple blockage or a component fault.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

I don't know if it's frost-free, sorry. I can't see any vent in the fridge part, and I'm not sure about a fan. It's a Hotpoint HMCB 7030 AA. I can hear it running a lot though. No burning smell or tripping.

Since you can't see vents and aren't sure if it's frost-free, let's start with the simplest possibilities. 1. Check the thermostat: Ensure the temperature control dial inside the fridge isn't set to '0' or off, and try turning it down one notch (e.g., from 4 to 3) to see if it cools better.
2. Clear the back wall: Even without visible vents, air flows through gaps at the back of the fridge liner. Please ensure no food containers are pressed against this back panel. If these don't help, we will need to look for signs of a fan or defrost issue.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
The dial is on 3 of 5 already. I can't see any vent at the back of the fridge part, but nothing is pressed against the back wall that I know of. Should I turn the dial up or down?

Turn the dial down to a lower number (e.g., towards 1 or 2) to make it colder; higher numbers usually mean warmer settings on most dials. However, given that your fridge is at 10°C while the freezer is fine, this suggests an airflow blockage rather than just a setting issue. In many integrated models like yours, cold air from the freezer passes into the fridge through a hidden channel behind the back panel. If ice builds up there (often due to a defrost fault), it blocks that air. Please perform a full manual defrost: switch the unit off at the wall socket, remove all food, leave both doors open for 24 hours until any internal ice has melted, then dry everything thoroughly and restart. This will tell us if the issue is temporary blockage or a deeper fault.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
Ok thanks. A full defrost means emptying everything and I haven't tried that yet. Is it definitely worth doing that first? There's only a bit of frost on the freezer back wall, not loads.

Yes, it is most likely worth doing. The 'bit of frost' you see on the freezer back wall is likely just the start of a blockage; if that ice spreads behind the panel into the fridge section, it chokes the airflow and causes exactly the 10°C temperature you're seeing. Since you can't dismantle the unit to check for hidden ice, the full defrost is the only way to clear any blockage in the internal channels. If it cools properly after this but warms up again in a few days, we will know there is a faulty defrost component that needs an engineer to replace.
Ok, I'll give the defrost a go then. Is there anything I should do with the food while it's off, since the freezer stuff would thaw?

Yes, please move the freezer items into cool bags or a cooler box with ice packs if you have them. For the fresh food in the fridge section, it’s best to eat perishable items (like dairy, meat, and leftovers) immediately before you switch the unit off. If you can’t eat them right away, put those items into a cooler box with ice packs as well. Once everything is out, wipe down any spilled water, leave both doors open for 24 hours, then dry it thoroughly before switching it back on.

candidates: Airflow blockage or incorrect temperature setting (high)
Faulty evaporator fan motor (not circulating cold air to fridge) (medium)
Defrost system failure causing ice blockage in the vent (medium)
